title: El Segundo
name: El Segundo
metaTitle: El Segundo in Los Angeles, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for El Segundo aerospace and R&D office, single-tenant corporate headquarters, and LAX-adjacent logistics space.

sections.html: El Segundo built its commercial base on aerospace and refining, and that legacy still shapes a market now split between legacy industrial and office campuses, a cluster of corporate headquarters, and a smaller technology-tenant wave pulled in from the South Bay coastline. An exchange buyer here needs a clear read on which of those three drivers a specific building actually depends on.

sections.heading: A Refinery and Aerospace Corridor Still in Use
sections.html:
The Chevron refinery on the city's western edge remains a major industrial presence, and the aerospace and defense contractors historically clustered around El Segundo's business parks continue to lease large-floor-plate office and R&D space built to specifications those tenants require. A replacement buyer looking at this corridor should confirm whether a specific building's mechanical and power infrastructure was built for a specialized aerospace or defense tenant, since that build-out can add or subtract value depending on the next tenant's use.

Some of these R&D buildings also carry clean-room space, reinforced floor loading, or secure-access requirements tied to defense contract work, and a buyer should ask directly whether any government security clearance requirements attach to the space itself rather than only to the current tenant's operations, since that distinction affects how quickly a building can re-lease to a new occupant.

sections.heading: Corporate Headquarters Office Space
sections.html:
El Segundo has attracted a number of corporate headquarters tenants over the years, drawn by lower office rents than the Westside combined with easy access to Los Angeles International Airport just to the north. These headquarters-style leases tend to run longer than a typical multi-tenant office building, which can make a single-tenant El Segundo building either a very stable replacement property or a concentrated credit risk, depending entirely on the tenant in place.

Corporate campus buildings in this submarket are often customized to a specific tenant's branding and floor-plan needs, with executive suites, large training rooms, or cafeteria space built out well beyond what a generic office user would require. A replacement buyer should budget for the possibility that a departing headquarters tenant leaves behind improvements that need significant reconfiguration before a new occupant can use the space efficiently, since demolition and re-tenanting costs on a heavily customized floor plate can run well above a standard office turnover budget.

sections.heading: LAX Proximity and Airport-Adjacent Logistics
sections.html: El Segundo's location just south of Los Angeles International Airport supports a logistics and flex-space market serving air-cargo-adjacent tenants, similar in function to Burbank's airport-area cluster but larger in scale given LAX's size relative to Hollywood Burbank Airport. Buyers should expect this inventory to price closer to conventional South Bay industrial product than to the specialized aerospace R&D space nearby.

sections.heading: The El Segundo Identification Set
sections.html:
A realistic El Segundo list draws from:

  • legacy aerospace and defense office and R&D buildings
  • single-tenant corporate headquarters office space
  • LAX-adjacent logistics and flex buildings
  • smaller technology-tenant office space converted from older industrial stock

sections.heading: Underwriting a Single-Tenant Concentration
sections.html:
Because so much of El Segundo's office inventory leases to one large tenant per building rather than a diversified roster, a replacement buyer should treat tenant credit and lease-term analysis as the central underwriting task rather than a secondary check. A qualified intermediary and lender both familiar with single-tenant corporate and aerospace leasing in this market will move faster than one applying assumptions modeled on a typical multi-tenant Los Angeles office building.

A single-tenant building also concentrates re-leasing risk at one point in time rather than spreading it across a rolling schedule of smaller leases, so a buyer should weigh the current tenant's remaining lease term heavily against the hold period they expect for the replacement property. A short remaining term on a specialized aerospace building can mean a longer, more uncertain re-leasing search than a comparable multi-tenant building would face.

faqs.q: Is El Segundo still an active aerospace and industrial market?
faqs.a: Yes. The Chevron refinery remains a major industrial presence, and aerospace and defense contractors continue to lease large-floor-plate office and R&D space in the city's business parks.

faqs.q: Why do corporate headquarters find El Segundo attractive?
faqs.a: Lower office rents than the Westside combined with easy access to Los Angeles International Airport have drawn a number of corporate headquarters tenants to the city over the years, and several campus buildings were customized heavily for a single tenant's branding and operational needs.

faqs.q: How does El Segundo's LAX-adjacent logistics space compare to Burbank's airport cluster?
faqs.a: It serves a similar air-cargo-adjacent function but at a larger scale, given LAX's size relative to Hollywood Burbank Airport, and it tends to price closer to conventional South Bay industrial product than to specialized aerospace R&D space in the same city.

faqs.q: What is the main underwriting risk in El Segundo office space?
faqs.a: Single-tenant concentration. Many buildings lease to one large corporate or aerospace tenant rather than a diversified roster, so tenant credit and lease-term analysis should be the central underwriting task, and a buyer should model a longer re-leasing period than a diversified building would typically require.

faqs.q: Should a buyer confirm building infrastructure before replacing into an aerospace-use building?
faqs.a: Yes. Confirm whether the mechanical and power infrastructure was built for a specialized aerospace or defense tenant, since that build-out can add or subtract value significantly depending on the next tenant's intended use, and check whether any security clearance requirements attach to the space itself.
